title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-06-24
content:
Week: 2026-06-22 -> 2026-06-26
Owners: Ravi Patel (kernel lead), Elena Morales (KV cache), Jordan Kim (batching)
Context: Continuation of kernel refactors and KV cache stabilization work that started in June. Goal this sprint was to land the fused-attention hot path, stabilize prefix/KV eviction heuristics, and improve dynamic batching tail latency for medium-seq workloads.

Highlights:
- Landed fused multi-head attention kernel prototype into canary pool (PR #1423). Early numbers show ~1.6-1.9x throughput uplift on Llama2-13B-like layers at seq_len=512 with 8 token beam workloads. p95 generation latency improved ~12% for these cases.
- KV cache memory compaction (compact-on-evict) merged (PR #1448). Observed ~24% reduction in resident memory on long-running chat sessions with many short-lived conversations.
- Dynamic batching improvements reduced p95 tail by ~25% for mixed small/medium requests (seq_len distribution 64/256/512) in our internal latency rig. The new adaptive batch timeout heuristic prevents large batch formation when load is spiky, without hurting sustained throughput.

Kernel work (Ravi):
- What shipped: fused-attention proto (xla-friendly codepaths) merged to canary. Unit/regression tests added for numeric parity at fp16/4-bit quant modes.
- Perf: microbenchmarks (dev-box A100x8) show 1.8x tokens/sec for seq_len=512 compared to baseline kernel, and 1.2x for seq_len=128. Memory transient allocations reduced by ~15% during forward-pass.
- Issues: occasional numerical drift at 4-bit quant + fused-kernel for very long sequences (>2048) — tracked in SR-3214. Working hypothesis: rounding differences in softmax reduction; mitigation options: higher-precision accumulation or selective fallback.
- Next: expand canary to 10% of traffic, add end-to-end safety tests for streaming and kv-cache interactions, and iterate on kernel fallback decision thresholds.

KV cache (Elena):
- What shipped: compact-on-evict logic + improved prefix dedup heuristics. Eviction now prefers whole-segment evict instead of per-token when reuse rate is low.
- Metrics: average KV memory per session dropped 24% on customer-sim workload, cache hit-rate improved from 68% -> 74% on multi-turn chat traces.
- Observability: added cache-hit tracing tags and per-request KV lookup latency breakdown to Console traces. Helps identify long-tail requests which caused repeated cache misses due to tokenization variance.
- Open problems: some customers still see high memory on extremely long-lived pinned contexts ( > 50k tokens). Need better offloading strategy or soft-eviction TTLs. Logged as SR-3228.
- Next: prototype partial offload to host DRAM for cold segments (+ bench), and add per-tenant cache sizing recommendation to Redwood Optimize.

Batching and routing (Jordan):
- What shipped: adaptive batch timeout heuristic (alpha release). It uses short-window latency + queue-depth signals to decide dynamic timeout per-worker.
- Perf: internal load tests (mixed qps) show p95 generation latency improved from ~420ms -> ~320ms for seq_len 256/512 mixes while maintaining >95% of baseline throughput. CPU utilization more stable.
- Observability: added per-route batching histograms in Console and a new flamegraph for worker-side batching delays.
- Rollout: progressive rollout to Dedicated pools this week. Monitoring alert if throughput drops >8% or p99 latency increases >15%.
- Risk: potential interaction with autoscaler burst policy causing transient undersizing — have a safety policy to fall back to static timeout if autoscaler signals scale-up in last 30s.

Standup / Meeting notes (daily logs):
- Mon 2026-06-22:
  - Kernel: initial canary rollout; smoke tests passed.
  - KV: compact-on-evict tests green. Noticed increased GC cycles in python shim when many small sessions killed — Elena to follow.
  - Batching: internal perf rig shows promising p95 improvements; will prepare canary config.

- Tue 2026-06-23:
  - Kernel: observed a couple of mismatch CPU-GPU paths under nightly fuzzing; created PR for accumulating in fp32 for softmax. (PR TODO linked in SR-3214)
  - KV: reproduced high mem case with synthetic long conversation; hypothesis that dedupe heuristic false-negative due to whitespace variants.
  - Batching: tuned adaptive alpha parameter; reran end-to-end tests.

- Wed 2026-06-24:
  - Cross-team sync: agreed rollout guardrails (circuit-breakers) and quick rollback plan.
  - Observability: Console team added batching flamegraph to dev tenant.
  - Action: Jordan to add unit test for worker timeout fallback.

- Thu 2026-06-25:
  - Kernel: rolled canary to 10% traffic; one customer session flagged slight quality regression in early morning window — investigating.
  - KV: implemented partial offload prototype to host DRAM (lab only). Initial results: memory reduction but 2-3% p95 latency penalty on cache miss path. Tradeoff analysis needed.
  - Batching: canary config deployed to Dedicated pools; monitoring dashboards created.

- Fri 2026-06-26:
  - Retrospective: cross-functional checklist worked well; rollbacks are quick. Need clearer SLIs for quantized kernel regressions.
  - Plan: focus next week on kernel numeric stability and KV offload perf tuning.

Blockers / Risks:
- Kernel numeric drift at 4-bit quant on very long sequences — needs prioritized investigation, may require partial fallback which reduces throughput gains.
- KV offload to host DRAM reduces memory but hurts cold-miss latency; need to evaluate per-tenant tradeoffs and integrate with routing policy.
- Autoscaler interactions with adaptive batching can produce short-term undersizing; mitigated via safety fallback but more testing required.

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: add fp32-accumulation fallback for softmax in fused kernel; target branch + perf run by 2026-07-01. (SR-3214)
- Elena: run perf sweep for host-DRAM offload prototype and produce cost/latency tradeoff doc (due 2026-07-02).
- Jordan: finalize unit tests for adaptive timeout fallback and wire up alerting thresholds (due 2026-06-30).
- Observability: instrument per-request KV lookup heatmap in Console for canary pools (Elena + Console team).

Notes / Misc (informal):
- "notes to self": we should add a small deterministic tokenizer normalization pass before KV lookup to reduce false-negative dedupe. Quick patch might buy time.
- Customer ask: enterprise-cust-7 requested lower p99 for long-chats; FYI they've been added to canary.
- Link to perf dashboards: internal-dashboard.redwood.ai/serving-runtime/canary-kernel-2026-06

Next week plan (high level):
- Stabilize fused kernel numeric behavior and widen canary if safe.
- Evaluate KV host-DRAM offload for a subset of non-latency-sensitive tenants.
- Continue batching rollout and monitor autoscaler interactions.
- Deliver a short doc for product describing per-tenant knobs (cache size, offload, batching aggressiveness) for Redwood Optimize integration.

Appendix: quick checklist for rollbacks and safety
- Canary rollback steps documented in runbook RBR-034 (Console link).
- Automated alerts: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput drop % and error-rate bump will trigger automated rollback if thresholds exceeded.

-- End of update --
